entry.title: Implementation of T+1 Settlement Cycle for Hong Kong Cash Market
entry.summary: HKSCC states that, subject to market readiness and regulatory approval, Hong Kong cash-market settlement will move from T+2 to T+1 in the second half of 2028. The circular asks Clearing Participants to assess T-day post-trade operations, liquidity and funding, client cut-offs and communications, customer documents, and exception controls.

entry.title: MAS Revokes the Major Payment Institution License of Sir Money Changer Pte Ltd
entry.summary: MAS revoked Sir Money Changer Pte. Ltd.'s Major Payment Institution Licence effective 15 September 2026 after finding that a third party independently operated a cross-border transfer business under its name and that the firm provided false or misleading information. MAS states that licensees must not allow third parties to use their licences and payment providers must maintain effective oversight and control.

entry.title: Motor finance legal challenge to be heard in February 2027
entry.summary: The FCA says challenges to its motor-finance compensation scheme will be heard from 16 to 26 February 2027. While the scheme is partly suspended, lenders must continue specified preparation and complaint activity; the FCA expects rigorous contingency planning, financial provisions and auditor engagement if the scheme or parts of it are quashed.

entry.title: Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence
entry.summary: HKMA issued updated ART supervisory guidance for all Authorized Institutions. Annex A supersedes the 2019 AI principles and expects proportionate governance across the AI lifecycle, including ownership, inventory, risk-based testing and monitoring, recovery, records, data and third-party safeguards, and fair and transparent customer use. HKMA states that policies, procedures and controls should be uplifted in a timely manner; no fixed deadline is stated. Annex B provides non-exhaustive Sandbox insights, while Annex C is preliminary and does not establish current agentic-AI requirements.

entry.title: Chongqing–Hong Kong Cross-boundary Data Validation Platform
entry.summary: HKMA announced the platform's launch for initial cross-boundary financial use cases, including account opening and loan applications. It verifies customer-presented data using blockchain technology and hash values without cross-boundary transfer or storage of original documents; the announcement states no participation requirement or timetable.

entry.title: MAS AI Risk Management Guidelines — operative document verified
entry.summary: MAS's final Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management apply to all financial institutions and all forms of AI as supervisory expectations. The reviewed operative document sets enterprise and use-case governance, board and senior-management accountability, inventories and materiality assessment, and proportionate lifecycle controls. Paragraphs 5.10–5.11 require risk-materiality-appropriate third-party AI controls and state that the FI retains primary accountability; where residual risk cannot be brought within risk appetite, the FI should consider limiting or suspending the service or replacing the provider. Paragraph 2.3 permits basic governance where poor performance or unavailability is unlikely to have a material adverse impact. Paragraph 1.8 sets 7 October 2027 for Sections 3–4 and 7 October 2028 for Sections 5–6. The official media release remains supporting evidence; the 30-page Guidelines are now the primary operative source.

entry.title: Circular to licensed corporations carrying out sponsor work and engaging in bookbuilding and placing activities
entry.summary: The SFC issued a supervisory circular for scoped sponsor, overall-coordinator and capital-market-intermediary roles, highlighting diligence, escalation, reporting and rejection of unresolved suspicious orders in IPO activity.

entry.title: SFC takes action against suspected IPO-rigging syndicates and suspends dealings in Baicha shares
entry.summary: The SFC directed a trading suspension and issued notice-specific asset restrictions to named brokers during an ongoing investigation into suspected IPO rigging; recipient brokers face immediate restriction and notification requirements.

entry.title: OCC Imposes $750 Million Assessment Against Bank of America for Deficient BSA/AML Compliance
entry.summary: The OCC issued a final consent order imposing a US$750 million civil money penalty on Bank of America for continuing BSA/AML-program deficiencies, providing an analogous non-binding control benchmark for Hong Kong firms.

entry.title: Practice Guide on Data Excellence
entry.summary: HKMA issued a Practice Guide on Data Excellence to all Authorized Institutions. It expects AIs to take its industry good practices into account when strengthening risk-data management across governance and accountability, data-quality management and control, and data infrastructure; the Guide creates no separate prescriptive requirement or mandated model.

entry.title: SFC approves six securities registrars for upcoming uncertificated securities market regime
entry.summary: The uncertificated securities market regime takes effect on 16 November 2026. The SFC approved six securities registrars effective that date; listed issuers of prescribed securities must maintain an approved registrar, and existing prescribed securities constituted under Bermuda, Cayman Islands, Mainland China or Hong Kong law have five years to participate.

entry.title: SFC approves six securities registrars for upcoming uncertificated securities market regime
entry.summary: The SFC approved six securities registrars effective 16 November 2026, when the USM regime takes effect. Listed issuers of prescribed securities must maintain an approved registrar; the stated requirements apply to issuers and registrars, not every bank.

entry.title: SFC proceeds to strengthen targeted tools to tackle IPO-related and other corporate misconduct
entry.summary: The SFC will proceed with proposed Stock Market Listing Rules and related Securities and Futures Ordinance amendments, with expected commencement in the first quarter of 2027 subject to the legislative process. This is an announced rule-change process, not a current final obligation.

entry.title: MAS AI Risk Management Guidelines — omitted finding correction
entry.summary: MAS's official 7 October 2026 PDF announces final AI Risk Management Guidelines for all financial institutions and all forms of AI. It describes supervisory expectations for board and senior-management accountability; AI-use inventories and materiality assessment; proportionate controls across data governance, testing, human oversight, cybersecurity, monitoring and change management; and accountability and assurance for third-party AI. Existing governance may be used where adequate, and a dedicated AI committee is not inherently required. If third-party AI risks cannot be brought within risk appetite, an FI should consider limiting, suspending or replacing the service. Basic governance may be proportionate where AI failure or unavailability is unlikely to have material impact on the FI, customers or other stakeholders. Sections 3–4 take effect on 7 October 2027 and Sections 5–6 by 7 October 2028; MAS intends to consult in 2027 on possible additional agentic-AI guidance. The operative Guidelines and response-to-feedback paper remained unavailable behind MAS maintenance content, so this correction makes no unsupported subsection-level claim.

entry.title: Project Liquidity: Engineering the Market Plumbing that Unlocks Capital Flows for Hong Kong
entry.summary: The SFC published a speech describing implemented and prospective HKEX clearing, collateral and settlement initiatives, including a March 2027 client-margin phase-2 target subject to regulatory approval. It is an official market-development signal, not a binding direction; final HKEX approvals, scope and terms remain to be published.

entry.title: SFC, AFRC and the Exchange join forces to address disclaimers of opinion solely relating to going concern
entry.summary: The SFC, AFRC and the Exchange issued a joint statement setting supervisory expectations for listed issuers with audit disclaimers solely relating to going concern. It expects robust assessments supported by reasonable assumptions, reliable data and feasible action plans, alongside detailed annual and quarterly progress disclosures and critical audit-committee and auditor review. The statement does not amend Listing Rules or set a new deadline; the Exchange may consider rule changes if improvement is not significant.

entry.title: Consultation Conclusions on Proposed Amendments to the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds
entry.summary: The SFC’s final-form proposed Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds Code amendments are tentatively effective on 1 November 2026 following gazettal; new schemes would comply at effectiveness and existing schemes generally have 12 months for specified liquidity, MMF and offering-document changes.

entry.title: LCQ17: Accelerated settlement for cash market
entry.summary: The Hong Kong Government says HKEX is preparing a proposed T+1 cash-market settlement cycle and targets consultation conclusions and implementation arrangements within 2026; no final implementation date or participant requirements are stated.

entry.title: SFST articulates Hong Kong's gold master plan at Global Precious Metals Conference
entry.summary: FSTB reports that the trial Hong Kong Gold Central Clearing and Settlement System has 11 banks as provisional direct participants and is scheduled for formal launch in Q1 2027, without mandating bank participation or setting a final rulebook.

entry.title: Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Bank Negara Malaysia Strengthen Bilateral Cooperation
entry.summary: HKMA and Bank Negara Malaysia announced bilateral workstreams on compliant cross-border stablecoin use cases, tokenisation and digital money, SME trade-finance data, cyber resilience, RTGS connectivity and possible central securities depository linkage. The announcement states collaboration and exploration, not a participation mandate, technical specification or implementation timetable for authorised institutions.
